headers.description: Optional headers to send with the request as a dictionary of header values.

Content-Type.description: The media type of the resource being requested, typically 'application/json'.

Authorization.description: The credentials to authenticate a user agent with a server, typically formatted as 'Bearer {token}'.

timeout.description: The maximum amount of time to wait for a response from the server, in seconds. A longer timeout may be necessary for slower network connections or overloaded servers. This is a float type value.

params.description: URL parameters to append to the URL. Sent as a dictionary of key-value pairs.

query.description: The query parameter for search or filtering.

page.description: The page number parameter for pagination. Used to retrieve a specific page of results.

auth.description: HTTP authentication credentials formatted as a (username, password) tuple.

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem), if required for the request.

cookies.description: Cookies to send with the request as a dictionary of cookie names and values.

sessionid.description: Session identifier cookie, used to recognize client sessions on the server.

csrftoken.description: CSRF protection token cookie, used to prevent cross-site request forgery attacks.

proxies.description: Proxy settings as a dictionary, mapping protocol or protocol and hostname to the URL of the proxy.

http.description: Proxy URL to use for HTTP requests, including the port number.

https.description: Proxy URL to use for HTTPS requests, including the port number.

stream.description: Whether to stream the download of the response. If False, the response content will be immediately downloaded. Streaming is useful for handling large files or responses.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not. Set to False to skip certificate verification, which is not recommended unless you are sure of the server's identity.

message.content:
Below is a quick‑start guide to a few popular IP‑lookup APIs that expose **company / organization** data (and often contact details such as email, phone, or website).  
All of them accept a plain IPv4/IPv6 address as a query parameter and return JSON.  
Pick the one that best fits your budget, rate‑limit needs, and data depth.

| Service | Endpoint | Key Data Returned | Free Tier | Notes |
|---------|----------|-------------------|-----------|-------|
| **ipinfo.io** | `https://ipinfo.io/<IP>/json` | `org`, `hostname`, `company` (name, domain, phone, email, logo) | 50k requests/month | Requires API key for company data; free tier gives only `org`. |
| **ipapi.com** | `https://ipapi.co/<IP>/json/` | `org`, `asn`, `company` (name, domain, phone, email) | 30k requests/month | API key optional for free tier; company data requires key. |
| **ipstack.com** | `http://api.ipstack.com/<IP>?access_key=YOUR_KEY&fields=ip,hostname,company` | `company` (name, domain, phone, email, logo) | 10k requests/month | Full company data only with paid plan. |
| **ipgeolocation.io** | `https://api.ipgeolocation.io/ipgeo?apiKey=YOUR_KEY&ip=<IP>` | `organization`, `company` (name, domain, phone, email, logo) | 1000 requests/day | Good for detailed corporate info. |
| **ipdata.co** | `https://api.ipdata.co/<IP>?api-key=YOUR_KEY` | `organization`, `company` (name, domain, phone, email, logo) | 1000 requests/day | Rich data set, includes contact details. |

---

## 1. ipinfo.io – The “Company” Endpoint

### Request

```http
GET https://ipinfo.io/8.8.8.8/json?token=YOUR_TOKEN
```

### Response (sample)

```json
{
  "ip": "8.8.8.8",
  "hostname": "dns.google",
  "city": "Mountain View",
  "region": "California",
  "country": "US",
  "loc": "37.3860,-122.0840",
  "org": "AS15169 Google LLC",
  "company": {
    "name": "Google LLC",
    "domain": "google.com",
    "phone": "+1-650-253-0000",
    "email": "contact@google.com",
    "logo": "https://ipinfo.io/static/img/company/google.png"
  }
}
```

> **Tip:** The `company` field is only populated when you have a paid plan (starting at $1/month). The free tier only returns the `org` string.

---

## 2. ipapi.com – Organization & Company

### Request

```http
GET https://ipapi.co/8.8.8.8/json/
```

### Response (sample)

```json
{
  "ip": "8.8.8.8",
  "city": "Mountain View",
  "region": "California",
  "country_name": "United States",
  "org": "AS15169 Google LLC",
  "asn": "15169",
  "company": {
    "name": "Google LLC",
    "domain": "google.com",
    "phone": "+1-650-253-0000",
    "email": "contact@google.com"
  }
}
```

> **Note:** The free tier (30k requests/month) returns `org` and `asn`. Company details require an API key.

---

## 3. ipstack.com – Company Data

### Request

```http
GET http://api.ipstack.com/8.8.8.8?access_key=YOUR_KEY&fields=ip,hostname,company
```

### Response (sample)

```json
{
  "ip": "8.8.8.8",
  "hostname": "dns.google",
  "company": {
    "name": "Google LLC",
    "domain": "google.com",
    "phone": "+1-650-253-0000",
    "email": "contact@google.com",
    "logo": "https://api.ipstack.com/static/img/company/google.png"
  }
}
```

> **Important:** The `company` field is only available on paid plans (starting at $9/month).

---

## 4. ipgeolocation.io – Organization + Contact

### Request

```http
GET https://api.ipgeolocation.io/ipgeo?apiKey=YOUR_KEY&ip=8.8.8.8
```

### Response (sample)

```json
{
  "ip": "8.8.8.8",
  "hostname": "dns.google",
  "city": "Mountain View",
  "region": "California",
  "country_name": "United States",
  "organization": "AS15169 Google LLC",
  "company": {
    "name": "Google LLC",
    "domain": "google.com",
    "phone": "+1-650-253-0000",
    "email": "contact@google.com",
    "logo": "https://api.ipgeolocation.io/static/img/company/google.png"
  }
}
```

---

## 5. ipdata.co – Rich Corporate Info

### Request

```http
GET https://api.ipdata.co/8.8.8.8?api-key=YOUR_KEY
```

### Response (sample)

```json
{
  "ip": "8.8.8.8",
  "hostname": "dns.google",
  "city": "Mountain View",
  "region": "California",
  "country_name": "United States",
  "organization": "AS15169 Google LLC",
  "company": {
    "name": "Google LLC",
    "domain": "google.com",
    "phone": "+1-650-253-0000",
    "email": "contact@google.com",
    "logo": "https://api.ipdata.co/static/img/company/google.png"
  }
}
```

> **Free tier:** 1000 requests/day. Company data is included.

---

## How to Choose

| Factor | ipinfo.io | ipapi.com | ipstack.com | ipgeolocation.io | ipdata.co |
|--------|-----------|-----------|-------------|------------------|-----------|
| **Free tier** | 50k/month (org only) | 30k/month (org only) | 10k/month (org only) | 1000/day (org+company) | 1000/day (org+company) |
| **Company data** | Paid plan | Paid plan | Paid plan | Free tier | Free tier |
| **Contact fields** | name, domain, phone, email, logo | name, domain, phone, email | name, domain, phone, email, logo | name, domain, phone, email, logo | name, domain, phone, email, logo |
| **Rate limit** | 50k/month | 30k/month | 10k/month | 1000/day | 1000/day |
| **Ease of use** | Simple JSON | Simple JSON | Simple JSON | Simple JSON | Simple JSON |

If you only need the **organization** string (`ASxxxx Company Name`) the free tiers of ipinfo.io or ipapi.com will do.  
If you need **contact details** (phone, email, logo), you’ll need a paid plan on most services, or you can use ipgeolocation.io or ipdata.co which include those fields even in their free tier.

---

## Quick Python Example (using `requests`)

```python
import requests

IP = "8.8.8.8"
API_KEY = "YOUR_KEY"

url = f"https://api.ipdata.co/{IP}"
params = {"api-key": API_KEY}

resp = requests.get(url, params=params, timeout=5)
data = resp.json()

print("IP:", data.get("ip"))
print("Organization:", data.get("organization"))
print("Company Name:", data.get("company", {}).get("name"))
print("Phone:", data.get("company", {}).get("phone"))
print("Email:", data.get("company", {}).get("email"))
```

Replace the URL and parameters with the service you choose.

---

### Final Checklist

1. **Sign up** for an API key on the chosen platform.  
2. **Read the docs** for rate limits and field availability.  
3. **Implement** the endpoint in your code (or use a library if available).  
4. **Handle errors** (e.g., 429 Too Many Requests, 400 Bad Request).  
5. **Cache** results if you hit the same IPs repeatedly to stay within limits.

Happy coding! If you need help wiring this into a specific stack (Node, Go, etc.) just let me know.
